Hi Emma / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the thoughtful questions from the payments and security teams. As discussed, to move from POC to pilot we need a couple of compliance clarifications so our Legal/Security teams can do a quick intake: 

1) Data role: can you confirm whether ClearlyPay will sign as Controller for customer data and will require Redwood to act as Processor? If you have an internal statement that captures that, please attach.
2) DPA: please confirm the appropriate recipient for a DPA (legal@clearlypay.com or procurement@clearlypay.com) so we can send our standard template.
3) SCC preference: do you have a preference for the SCC module flavor (Module 1/Controller, Module 2/Processor, Module 3/Joint) or do you want us to propose the Processor-focused variant?
4) SOC 2: what is your expected timeline for SOC 2 in-scope requirements for vendors? Any existing reports or attestation links would be helpful.
5) Vendor SQ: I wasn’t able to finish the questionnaire on the call — can you send the vendor security questionnaire (we’ll populate and return).

Next steps I propose: I will loop in Security & Legal internally (cc’d Laura and Ben) and send our DPA template and a recommended SCC module based on your controller confirmation. Can you send the vendor questionnaire and indicate who should receive the DPA?

If helpful, happy to set a 30-min compliance sync with your security contact this week.

Best,

Thanks for the heads-up, Markus. Quick intake from Security: 

- Controller/Processor: Agreed — ClearlyPay = Controller; Redwood = Processor. We'll propose Module 2 (Processor) SCC variant and include a short addendum covering data segmentation and retention for payment tokens. That should address the payments-specific concerns without creating joint-controller exposure.
- PCI language: We should add an explicit paragraph limiting Redwood's scope to non-PCI PAN processing unless customer routes raw PAN to Redwood. If they need PAN-level processing, we'll require a separate SOW and PCI scoping conversation.
- SOC 2: Q1 2027 timeline is acceptable. We'll offer to provide our latest SOC 2 Type 2 report (redacted) under an NDA and note expected cadence for full attestation.
- Vendor SQ: Stephanie, please complete the questionnaire. I'll review the security responses and prepare a cover memo summarizing anything that needs remediation or follow-up.
